title: FactPack
description: Agent A's (A1 Evidence Collection / A2 Verified Claim Registry) evidence boundary between research and storytelling. producer_outline.json may only cite claim_ids that exist here; final_script.json narration may only assert claims marked allowed_in_narration.

status.description: pending: not started. collected: A1 evidence collection done. verified: A2 adversarial pass done, allowed_in_narration values are trustworthy.

research_language.description: Snapshot of the channel's research_language at collection time (research itself may draw on sources in any language)

working_language.description: Snapshot of the channel's working_language -- normalized_claim text is written in this language for internal consistency

quirk_lead.description: The episode_brief's quirk, carried forward as a research lead only. It is NOT a claim and must never be treated as pre-verified or auto-promoted to the thesis.

note.default: Research lead only -- not a verified fact. Must not be assumed as the thesis until supported by claims in this fact pack.

claims.description: Atomic, independently traceable claims. A claim must be small enough that one confidence value and one allowed_in_narration value apply coherently to the WHOLE claim -- if part of it is solid and part is shaky, split it. Includes both sourced claims and derived_comparison claims (numbers computed from other claims -- see the numerical claim rule in agents/agent_a_producer_writer.md).

normalized_claim.description: ONE independently falsifiable assertion, stated plainly in working_language, independent of any beat's phrasing

time_context.description: The time period the claim is ABOUT, e.g. '1982', '1985-1987', '2007'. Not the publication date of the evidence -- that lives in each source's publication_date.

sources.description: Structured provenance, one entry per source. Source QUALITY (source_classification) and source ACCESSIBILITY (access_status) are independent: a strong source that could not be fetched stays strong but is marked unavailable; it does not become reference_only. May be empty for a derived_comparison claim, which cites source_claim_ids instead.

publication_date.description: When the EVIDENCE was published. Distinct from the claim's time_context.

source_classification.description: Intrinsic quality of the source, independent of whether it could be fetched. Wikipedia, Wikipedia mirrors, wikis, generic aggregators, spec-scraper sites and search-result snippets are reference_only by default and must never be classified high_quality_secondary.

access_status.description: How much of this source was actually read. search_snippet_only means only a search-engine summary was seen -- the page itself was never read.

evidence_note.description: Briefly, exactly what THIS source supports for THIS claim

evidence_location.description: Where in the source the evidence sits -- page, section, table, timestamp -- as specifically as possible

perspective.description: What era/viewpoint the CLAIM IS ABOUT -- never when the evidence page was published. A historical production or price figure compiled by a modern source is still contemporary (or timeless) to its era; the modern publication date belongs in the source's publication_date. Use retrospective only when the claim is itself a later judgment, reassessment or reputation formed after the fact.

confidence.description: unresolved claims cannot be stated as fact in narration -- allowed_in_narration must be false

allowed_in_narration.description: Whether this claim, as currently evidenced, may be asserted as fact in final_script.json. Must be false whenever confidence is 'unresolved'.

safe_wording.description: Pre-approved phrasing that does not overclaim beyond the evidence -- the wording a writer may use, or the hedge to use if allowed_in_narration is false

forbidden_or_unsupported_inference.description: Specific conclusions a writer might be tempted to draw from this claim that the evidence does NOT support

conflicting_evidence.description: Other data points/sources that disagree with this claim. Must be preserved here rather than silently resolved for narrative convenience; empty array if none.

source_claim_ids.description: Required (by convention, not schema) when claim_type is derived_comparison: the claim_ids the calculation is derived from

calculation.description: For derived_comparison claims: the literal arithmetic performed, e.g. '(12131 - 8499) / 8499 * 100'

result.description: For derived_comparison claims: the calculated result, stated with its comparator explicit
